subject: Re: LatticeWorks on-prem K8s deployment: architecture review & storage SLAs
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@latticeworks.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: LatticeWorks on-prem K8s deployment — initial ask

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this on. We are kicking off an internal review to validate that Redwood Private will meet our on-prem constraints. High level:
- Two clusters (prod / staging) across two racks in our DC (no shared storage between racks).
- Expected steady state: 24 pods serving inference, burst traffic up to 80 pods during peak windows.
- Storage: models live on a blockstore; we need fast reads (p95 < 12ms) and snapshot-based backups daily.
- Data residency and encryption: at-rest encryption with our KMS required; audit logs retained 365 days.

Can you outline the recommended cluster footprint, node profiles, and storage classes you think would satisfy both perf and SLA (we care about tail latency for token streaming)? Also include any procurement-level BOM items we should budget for.

We’ve attached our high-level DC constraints (attached: lattice_dc_constraints.pdf) — happy to walk through early next week.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Infra — LatticeWorks
Elena.Rossi@latticeworks.com

Elena — thanks for the clear constraints. I put together a concise agenda for a 45-minute architecture review and a preliminary recommendation below. Attaching: redwood_private_arch_diagram.pdf and prelim_bom.csv.

Proposed agenda (45m):
- 10m: Lattice constraints + DC topology (you)
- 15m: Redwood proposed cluster footprint + nodepool sizing (us)
- 10m: Storage class options, KMS/keys, and backup cadence (us)
- 10m: MAP (mutual action plan) and procurement path

Prelim recommendation (summary):
- Clusters: single-zone K8s per rack (2 clusters: prod, staging). Use node pools split by role: 
  - inference-gpu: 4 x p4-equivalent nodes (GPU-backed) for steady 24 pods, autoscale to 12 nodes for burst; isolate via nodeSelector/tolerations.
  - cpu-serv: 6 x c8-equivalent nodes for control, API, preproc pipelines; autoscale 6->10.
  - infra-svc: 2 small nodes for monitoring/sidecars and CSI controllers.
- Storage: local NVMe for GPU cache (ephemeral), and replicated blockstore for model artifacts (CSI-rbd or iSCSI LVM depending on existing infra). We recommend a dedicated PV class backed by the blockstore with read-optimized policy and tuned fsync settings for streaming workloads.
- KMS: Redwood integrates with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud KMS proxy; we will require a key rotation window and IAM mapping.
- Backups: snapshot to object storage nightly + incremental replicas to an offsite for 30-day retention.

Open items we need from you before the call:
- exact rack boundaries and VLAN isolation details
- existing blockstore vendor and iSCSI/NFS endpoints
- permissable egress windows for RMQ/telemetry

Does Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 PT work for an initial call? I’ll draft a MAP after we sync.

—
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: LatticeWorks on-prem K8s deployment — architecture notes

Elena / team — quick notes ahead of the call, focused on risk and operational controls: 

Operational risk & mitigations:
- Cross-rack failure: do not rely on a single PV class that spans racks. If your blockstore supports replication across racks, we can expose a PV class with topology-aware provisioning; otherwise plan for async replication between racks.
- Cold-starts for large model loads: plan a small warm pool of preloaded pods per inference-gpu node to avoid cache-thrashing on bursts.
- Eviction policy: set kube-eviction thresholds conservatively (memory.available margin) and use PodDisruptionBudgets for core inference services.

Security / compliance:
- KMS: require an HSM-backed key or Cloud KMS proxy with strict IAM roles. We can document key usage per cluster in the MAP.
- Audit logs: we recommend forwarding audit logs to your SIEM; Redwood can ship canonical audit payloads to an on-prem collector or to an S3-compatible endpoint in your controlled account.

Storage-class guidance (short):
- Hot reads: CSI-rbd or NVMe-backed local cache + read-through layer. Tuned readahead and blk-mq settings for p95 targets.
- Model artifacts: compressed, chunked artifacts served from blockstore with async prefetch into local NVMe cache.

I’ll bring a short checklist for the call listing ports, CIDR ranges, and required service accounts.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

- Can you confirm support for our KMS vendor (Thales) and whether Redwood requires additional licensing for the private control plane?

Also: can you produce a brief mutual action plan (MAP) that ties deliverables to dates (site prep, network handoff, image bake, on-site install, verification)? If you can circulate a draft before Tue’s meeting, that will speed internal approvals.

Elena

Elena — attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP_LW_v1.xlsx) and a one-page rollout checklist in the GDrive link. Key milestones:
- Site prep & VLAN allocation (Owner: LatticeWorks) — target 2026-11-20
- Network handoff & firewall rules (Owner: LatticeWorks / Redwood) — target 2026-11-25
- Image bake & validation (Owner: Redwood) — target 2026-12-02
- On-site install & smoke tests (Owner: Redwood) — target 2026-12-08 to 2026-12-10

Notes / assumptions:
- We assume an offsite S3-compatible endpoint for nightly snapshots and a reachable KMS proxy endpoint.
- Procurement: for guaranteed burst capacity we recommend a 12-month reserved capacity for the inference-gpu pool — will provide cost options in the follow-up.

If that looks reasonable I’ll lock time for Tue 2026-11-09 10:00 PT and prepare a short deck.
